headline: High-risk filesystem and data-flow mismatch: ChatGPT Desktop can read user files/screens while ms-swift can write and execute code, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app content by default, while ms-swift can read/write files and process stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if ms-swift outputs are copied into ChatGPT or shared via files. No shared MCP exists, so this is not high.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is copied into ChatGPT Desktop as a file, clipboard item, or pasted text
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to interpret ms-swift-generated logs, configs, or prompts as instructions
mitigations: Use a separate review step for ms-swift outputs before pasting into ChatGPT
Disable clipboard bridging during analysis sessions
Keep ms-swift outputs in a read-only folder
Prefix untrusted ms-swift artifacts with a warning banner
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files, and ChatGPT Desktop explicitly touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files. If they share a workspace or the same sensitive corpus, either agent can surface data into the other’s outputs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, dataset, or project workspace
IF sensitive files are uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop while ms-swift can read the same workspace
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Move sensitive files out of shared directories
Restrict ChatGPT uploads to sanitized copies
Restrict ms-swift to non-sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files and interact with supported apps. If both operate on the same directory, ms-swift can overwrite artifacts that ChatGPT later reads or summarizes. The write/read overlap plus unrestricted local execution makes conflict dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem path or project checkout
IF ms-swift writes artifacts that ChatGPT Desktop later reads or summarizes
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Make ChatGPT inputs read-only copies
Run ms-swift in a disposable environment
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
requires-engineering: add file locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce summaries from files and app context, and ms-swift can consume and transform those outputs through CLI/Python workflows. If ms-swift treats ChatGPT-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream configs, checkpoints, or evaluation outputs. The pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking.
conditions: IF ms-swift ingests ChatGPT-generated summaries without verification
IF ChatGPT output is used as the source for configs, prompts, or evaluation inputs
mitigations: Require human review before ms-swift consumes ChatGPT output
Add checksum or diff checks on generated artifacts
Keep ChatGPT output in a draft-only folder
Compare outputs against source files before execution
requires-engineering: add validation gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data plus hub tokens. If regulated or personal data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not state matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed by both agents in the same workflow
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to logs, checkpoints, or uploaded files
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Separate retention buckets for ChatGPT and ms-swift artifacts
Redact personal data before processing
Document data-handling responsibilities per agent
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
